verdict.rationale: Kick ships a native Rules feature that lets users define their own logic for handling transactions. Rules run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs, and AI-native users can create them through the MCP connectors. Missing for 10: documentation of trigger events beyond transaction sync and of actions beyond categorization overrides, details on rule conditions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Rules let you tell Kick exactly how to handle specific transactions - overriding AI categorization with your own logic.
Once a rule is created, it runs automatically every time a matching transaction syncs.
Rules override AI categorization and run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs.
Query transactions, generate reports, create automation rules, and execute bookkeeping changes
